topics.name: used to / would for past habits
Phrasal verbs (put up with, set out, get rid of)

options: Amit is more stronger than Yatin.
questions.rule: To compare two people, add -er and use than: stronger than. Never use more with -er.

options: Dick use to sleep in the attic.
Dick used to slept in the attic.
Dick used to sleep in the attic.
questions.rule: A past habit is used to + base verb: used to sleep.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: the ... in the whole city needs the superlative. bad - worse - worst.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The phrase is get rid of (remove something unwanted): got rid of the rats.
than compares two places, so use the comparative: bigger.
For a habit in the past, use used to + base verb: I used to play.
"I have no home" becomes he had no home: the pronoun and the tense both change after said.

chat: Did you live in a village as a child?
options: Yes, I used to live near a farm.
Yes, I use to live near a farm.
Yes, I used to living near a farm.
questions.rule: Past habit or state: used to + base verb: I used to live.

chat: Is your new school bigger than the old one?
options: Yes, it is much biggest than the old one.
Yes, it is more bigger than the old one.
Yes, it is much bigger than the old one.
questions.rule: Two schools are compared, so use bigger than. much can make a comparative stronger.

options: Dick said that I was hungry.
Dick said that he was hungry.
Dick said that he were hungry.
questions.rule: I becomes he, and after said the present am moves back to was.

options: The cook told Dick to go away.
The cook told Dick that go away.
The cook told to Dick to go away.
questions.rule: A reported command is told + person + to + verb: told Dick to go away.

options: Please look for after my cat while I am away.
Please look after my cat while I am away.
Please look after of my cat while I am away.
questions.rule: look after means take care of. It needs no extra word: look after my cat.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: would for a past habit is followed by the base verb, for both actions: would wake ... and take.

questions.before: Alice asked her father if she
questions.rule: After asked, can moves back to could in reported speech.

questions.after: for London early the next morning.
questions.rule: set out means start a journey: set out for London.
Longer adjectives form the comparative with more: more alarmed than.

chat: What did the carter ask Dick?
options: He asked Dick if he was running away from home.
He asked Dick if was he running away from home.
He asked Dick that was he running away from home.
questions.rule: A reported yes/no question uses if and normal word order: if he was running away.

chat: How did you get rid of the mosquitoes?
options: We got rid from them with a net.
We got rid them with a net.
We got rid of them with a net.
questions.rule: Always keep of in get rid of: we got rid of them.

questions.source: Dick was the poorest boy in the village.
options: Dick was poorer than any other boy in the village.
Dick was poorer than other any boy in the village.
Dick was more poorer than any other boy in the village.
questions.rule: Superlative the poorest becomes poorer than any other boy.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Both used to and would for past habits take the base verb: used to walk, would carry ... and sing.

options: This road is lesser crowded than that one.
This road is the less crowded than that one.
This road is less crowded than that one.
questions.rule: The opposite of more is less: less crowded than. Don't add the before a comparative with than.

options: The queen asked what did they call the animal.
The queen asked what they called the animal.
The queen asked what they call the animal?
questions.rule: A reported question has statement word order (they called), a past tense, and ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: When only two are compared, use the comparative: the cleverer one (of two).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A reported question needs a subject before could, so use the subject pronoun: whether she could buy the cat.
The phrase is look forward to + noun or -ing: looking forward to a good sleep.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about a past habit.
questions.rule: would + base verb shows a repeated action in the past: Dick would sit every evening.

chat: For a long trip, which is better, a bus or a train?
options: A train is more better than a bus.
A train is better than a bus.
A train is best than a bus.
questions.rule: good is irregular: good - better - best. Two things are compared: better than.

questions.source: The carter said to Dick, "Where are you going?"
options: The carter asked Dick where he was going.
The carter asked Dick where was he going.
The carter asked Dick where he were going.
questions.rule: Use asked, keep the question word, then statement order with the past: where he was going.

questions.source: Dick slept in an alley, but he does not now.
options: Dick use to sleep in an alley.
Dick used to sleep in an alley.
Dick used to slept in an alley.
questions.rule: Something true in the past but not now: used to + base verb: used to sleep.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: After replied, will moves back to would. After told + person + to, use the base verb: to feed.

options: Dick became richest than he had ever imagined.
Dick became richer than he had ever imagine.
Dick became richer than he had ever imagined.
questions.rule: than needs the comparative (richer), and the past perfect is had + past participle: had imagined.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: put out a fire means stop it burning. put on means wear or switch on.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A past state that is no longer true is used to + base verb: there used to be a tree.

questions.before: The queen asked the captain what the animal
questions.rule: After asked, the present is moves back to was: what the animal was called.
on the whole ship compares one with all the others, so use the superlative: good - better - the best.
In a reported question the subject comes before the verb: where I was going.

options: Sorry, sir, the bus broke down on the way.
Sorry, sir, the bus breaked down on the way.
Sorry, sir, the bus was broke down on the way.
questions.rule: break down = stop working. Its past is broke down (irregular), with no was.

questions.source: London was bigger than Dick's village.
options: Dick's village was not as big as London.
Dick's village was not as bigger as London.
Dick's village was not so big than London.
questions.rule: Comparative becomes not as + plain adjective + as: not as big as London.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using 'would' for a past habit.
questions.source: As a boy, Dick used to help the cook with the pots and pans.
options: As a boy, Dick would help the cook with the pots and pans.
As a boy, Dick would helped the cook with the pots and pans.
As a boy, Dick will help the cook with the pots and pans.
questions.rule: For repeated past actions, used to + verb can become would + base verb: would help.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: had ever seen needs a superlative (biggest); than needs dirtier; not as ... as takes the plain form: friendly.

options: She asked me whether I had finished my homework yet?
She asked me whether I had finished my homework.
She asked me whether had I finished my homework.
questions.rule: A reported question uses whether/if, statement order (I had finished) and a full stop, not ?.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: one of the + superlative is followed by a plural noun: one of the most popular men.

questions.after: with the pots and pans in the kitchen.
questions.rule: In get used to (= become familiar with), to is a preposition, so the -ing form follows: got used to working.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a phrasal verb.
questions.rule: put up with means tolerate. The three parts stay together: could not put up with the temper.

chat: What did Mr Joshi tell you?
options: He told me to bring my atlas tomorrow.
He told me bring my atlas tomorrow.
He said me to bring my atlas tomorrow.
questions.rule: A reported instruction: told + person + to + verb. said cannot take a person directly.

chat: Is Kolkata as crowded as Mumbai?
options: No, Mumbai is even most crowded than Kolkata.
No, Mumbai is even crowdeder than Kolkata.
No, Mumbai is even more crowded than Kolkata.
questions.rule: Long adjectives like crowded use more for comparing two: more crowded than.

questions.source: Mr Fitzwarren said to Dick, "Have you nothing of your own?"
options: Mr Fitzwarren asked Dick if he had nothing of his own.
Mr Fitzwarren asked Dick if he had nothing of your own.
Mr Fitzwarren asked Dick if had he nothing of his own.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if, statement order, have becomes had, your becomes his.

questions.source: Very few cats are as clever as Puss.
options: Puss is one of the most cleverest cats.
Puss is one of the cleverest cats.
Puss is one of the cleverest cat.
questions.rule: Very few ... as clever as becomes one of the cleverest + plural noun: cats.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: told takes an object pronoun (her); the story is past (said); advised + person + to + base verb (to worry).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: used to + base verb (sit); after told use the past perfect (had called); had ever heard needs the most.
